basis: Marrow mast-cell neoplasm; persistent skin infiltration ~70-80%; mast-cell-mediated bone loss ~30-50%, including osteopenia/osteoporosis.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: mast-cell-mediated osteopenia/osteoporosis affects approximately 30-50%; bone loss qualifies even without destructive focal lesions.

basis: Rickettsia sibirica infection; necrotic inoculation eschar occurs in approximately 80% and represents direct skin injury. Transient exanthem alone would not qualify.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: inoculation eschar is necrotic skin injury in approximately 80%, rather than merely a transient rash.

basis: Diabetes, deafness and developmental delay each 2/2; high myopia 1/2 supports ocular dysfunction. Scoliosis and alopecia, each 1/2, omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.ocular: involved: high myopia affects 1/2 reported patients, with functional visual impairment; small sample limits confidence.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none at cap: scoliosis occurs in 1/2, but unspecified severity gives it lower priority than high myopia and the three defining axes.

basis: Bile-acid synthesis defect with cholestatic liver injury. Malabsorption and coagulopathy (each 30-79%) reflect deficient bile, vitamin K or hepatic synthesis, without direct gut/blood injury.

decisions.haematologic: none: coagulopathy occurs in 30-79% but follows deficient hepatic factor synthesis/vitamin K; direct blood-cell or coagulation-system disease is not established.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: fat malabsorption occurs in 30-79% because bile acids are deficient; intrinsic intestinal damage or loss of intestinal function is not established.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment defines syndrome; supplied HPO reports aortic aneurysm in 80-99% and congenital diaphragmatic hernia, a structural skeletal-muscle defect, in 30-79%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: congenital diaphragmatic hernia occurs in 30-79% per supplied HPO and reflects a structural defect of skeletal muscle; hypotonia alone is insufficient.

basis: Liver-origin lymphoma occupies hepatic tissue, is a malignant lymphoid blood-cell disorder, and receives the required lymphoma mechanism axis.

decisions.haematologic: primary: lymphoma is a neoplasm of lymphoid blood cells even when its primary anatomical site is extranodal liver.

basis: Developmental impairment and hearing loss define syndrome (80-99%). Cardiac defects and cleft palate each have only singleton 1/1 observations; high palate alone does not establish damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiac abnormalities are reported in 1/1 assessed patient; a singleton does not establish prevalence of at least 30% across this syndrome.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: cleft palate is a singleton 1/1 observation, insufficient to establish at least 30%; frequent high palate and feeding difficulty alone do not demonstrate injury.

basis: Skull ossification defects 80-99%; cataract/eye malformations and cleft palate 30-79%. Listed CNS malformations individually 5-29%; hepatomegaly alone does not show hepatic damage.

decisions.neurologic: none: supplied CNS malformations individually occur in 5-29%; common neurologic dysfunction or a major neurologic diagnostic criterion is not established.

basis: Localized plasma-cell malignancy arising in chest-wall bone or supporting soft tissue. Plasmacytoma is a plasma-cell neoplasm; the broad lymphoma ancestor does not establish an immune mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: plasmacytoma is a plasma-cell neoplasm, not a lymphoma; the supplied lymphoma parent does not override its specific tumour identity.

basis: Macroglossia and omphalocele define this subtype; abdominal-wall muscular defects and somatic overgrowth support musculoskeletal. Transient hypoglycemia and tumour risks add no damaged organ.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: congenital abdominal-wall muscular defects, especially omphalocele, are core CDKN1C-related features; somatic overgrowth also characterizes the syndrome.
